title: Deep Reinforcement Learning for Autonomous Robot Navigation
abstract: This paper presents a deep reinforcement learning framework for autonomous navigation of mobile robots in dynamic and cluttered environments. We propose a novel reward shaping technique that accelerates convergence and improves policy stability. Extensive experiments in simulated and real world environments demonstrate that our approach outperforms classical path planning methods and prior learning based baselines in terms of success rate and collision avoidance. The proposed method generalizes well to unseen environments and shows robustness to sensor noise.

title: A Transformer Based Approach for Scientific Text Summarization
abstract: Automatic summarization of scientific literature is a challenging task due to the technical vocabulary and long document lengths involved. In this work we introduce a transformer based encoder decoder model fine tuned specifically for summarizing research papers. We evaluate our model on a large corpus of arXiv papers and show significant improvements over extractive and traditional abstractive baselines using ROUGE metrics. Human evaluation further confirms that the generated summaries are coherent and factually consistent with the source documents.

title: Convolutional Neural Networks for Medical Image Classification
abstract: Medical image classification plays a crucial role in computer aided diagnosis systems. In this study we design a convolutional neural network architecture optimized for classifying X-ray and MRI scans across multiple disease categories. Our model incorporates attention mechanisms to focus on clinically relevant regions of the image. Experimental results on multiple public medical imaging datasets show that our approach achieves state of the art accuracy while maintaining interpretability through visualization of attention maps.

title: Graph Neural Networks for Social Network Analysis
abstract: Graph neural networks have emerged as a powerful tool for modeling relational data such as social networks. This paper explores the application of graph convolutional networks to the tasks of community detection and link prediction in large scale social graphs. We propose a scalable training strategy that reduces memory consumption without sacrificing predictive performance. Our experiments on several benchmark social network datasets demonstrate superior performance compared to traditional graph embedding techniques.

title: Natural Language Inference Using Pretrained Language Models
abstract: Natural language inference is a fundamental task in natural language processing that requires determining the logical relationship between a premise and a hypothesis. We investigate the effectiveness of large pretrained transformer language models for this task and propose a fine tuning strategy that incorporates auxiliary linguistic features. Our experiments across several benchmark datasets show consistent improvements over baseline transformer models, particularly in cases involving negation and quantifier scope ambiguity.

title: Federated Learning for Privacy Preserving Healthcare Analytics
abstract: Federated learning enables collaborative model training across distributed healthcare institutions without sharing raw patient data, addressing critical privacy concerns. This paper proposes a federated learning framework tailored for heterogeneous electronic health record data. We introduce a personalization layer that adapts the global model to local data distributions at each institution. Experiments on multi institution clinical datasets show that our framework achieves comparable accuracy to centralized training while preserving patient privacy.

title: Explainable AI Methods for Credit Risk Assessment
abstract: As machine learning models are increasingly deployed in high stakes financial decisions, the need for explainability has become paramount. This work surveys and evaluates several explainable AI techniques applied to credit risk assessment models, including SHAP, LIME, and attention based interpretability methods. We conduct a comparative study on a real world lending dataset and analyze how well each method aligns with domain expert judgments regarding feature importance and decision rationale.

title: Attention Mechanisms in Speech Recognition Systems
abstract: Attention mechanisms have significantly advanced the performance of automatic speech recognition systems by allowing models to focus on relevant portions of the input sequence. In this paper we systematically compare different attention variants including additive, multiplicative, and multi head attention within an end to end speech recognition pipeline. Our results on standard speech benchmarks reveal that multi head attention provides the best trade off between recognition accuracy and computational efficiency.

title: Unsupervised Anomaly Detection in Time Series Data Using Autoencoders
abstract: Detecting anomalies in time series data is essential for applications ranging from industrial monitoring to fraud detection. We propose an unsupervised anomaly detection framework based on variational autoencoders that learns a compact latent representation of normal system behavior. Deviations from this learned representation are used to flag anomalous events. Experimental evaluation on multiple real world time series benchmarks demonstrates that our method achieves higher detection accuracy with fewer false positives compared to existing unsupervised approaches.

title: Robotic Grasping Using Deep Learning and Tactile Feedback
abstract: Reliable robotic grasping in unstructured environments remains a significant challenge in robotics research. This paper presents a deep learning framework that combines visual perception with tactile sensor feedback to improve grasp stability. We collect a large dataset of grasping attempts across diverse object shapes and materials to train our model. Real robot experiments show that incorporating tactile feedback substantially reduces grasp failures compared to vision only baselines.

title: Sentiment Analysis of Social Media Text Using Deep Learning
abstract: Sentiment analysis of social media content presents unique challenges due to informal language, slang, and short text length. This study proposes a hybrid deep learning model combining convolutional and recurrent layers to capture both local and sequential patterns in tweets. We evaluate our approach on several publicly available sentiment datasets and show that it outperforms traditional machine learning classifiers as well as standalone CNN and LSTM models.

title: Bayesian Optimization for Hyperparameter Tuning of Deep Neural Networks
abstract: Hyperparameter tuning is a critical yet computationally expensive step in training deep neural networks. This paper investigates the use of Bayesian optimization as an efficient alternative to grid search and random search for hyperparameter selection. We propose a surrogate model based on Gaussian processes combined with an acquisition function tailored for noisy objective evaluations. Experiments across several deep learning benchmarks demonstrate faster convergence to optimal hyperparameter configurations.

title: Semantic Segmentation of Satellite Imagery Using Deep Learning
abstract: Semantic segmentation of satellite imagery is important for applications such as land cover classification and urban planning. We propose a deep convolutional encoder decoder architecture with skip connections tailored to the multi spectral nature of satellite images. Our model is trained and evaluated on large scale remote sensing datasets, achieving improved segmentation accuracy for vegetation, water bodies, and built up areas compared to existing baseline architectures.

title: Multi Agent Reinforcement Learning for Traffic Signal Control
abstract: Efficient traffic signal control is essential for reducing urban congestion and emissions. This paper proposes a multi agent reinforcement learning framework in which each traffic signal is controlled by an independent learning agent that cooperates with neighboring agents through shared state information. Simulation results on a realistic urban traffic network show that our cooperative multi agent approach reduces average vehicle waiting time compared to independently trained agents and fixed time signal control baselines.

title: Knowledge Graph Embedding Techniques for Recommendation Systems
abstract: Knowledge graphs provide rich structured information that can enhance the performance of recommendation systems. In this work we survey several knowledge graph embedding techniques and evaluate their effectiveness when integrated into collaborative filtering based recommender models. Our experiments on benchmark recommendation datasets show that incorporating knowledge graph embeddings improves recommendation accuracy, particularly in cold start scenarios involving new users and items.

title: Adversarial Robustness of Deep Learning Models for Image Classification
abstract: Deep learning models for image classification are known to be vulnerable to adversarial perturbations that are imperceptible to humans. This paper studies several adversarial training techniques and evaluates their effectiveness at improving model robustness without significantly degrading clean accuracy. We conduct extensive experiments across multiple network architectures and adversarial attack methods, providing practical guidelines for training more robust image classification models.

title: Few Shot Learning for Text Classification in Low Resource Languages
abstract: Text classification in low resource languages is hindered by the scarcity of labeled training data. We propose a few shot learning approach that leverages cross lingual pretrained embeddings and meta learning to enable effective classification with only a handful of labeled examples per class. Experiments on multiple low resource language datasets demonstrate that our method significantly outperforms standard fine tuning approaches under limited data conditions.

title: Neural Machine Translation with Improved Handling of Rare Words
abstract: Neural machine translation systems often struggle with rare and out of vocabulary words, leading to degraded translation quality. This paper proposes a subword segmentation strategy combined with a copy mechanism that allows the model to directly transfer rare words from source to target sentences when appropriate. Evaluation on multiple language pairs shows consistent improvements in translation quality, particularly for domains with specialized or technical vocabulary.

title: Time Series Forecasting Using Long Short Term Memory Networks
abstract: Accurate time series forecasting is critical for applications such as demand planning and financial market analysis. This paper evaluates the performance of long short term memory networks for multivariate time series forecasting and compares them against traditional statistical models such as ARIMA. Our experiments on multiple real world datasets show that LSTM based models capture complex temporal dependencies more effectively, particularly for series exhibiting nonlinear and long range patterns.

title: Data Augmentation Strategies for Improving Deep Learning Model Generalization
abstract: Data augmentation is a widely used technique to improve the generalization ability of deep learning models, particularly when training data is limited. This paper presents a systematic comparison of various data augmentation strategies including geometric transformations, mixup, and generative adversarial network based augmentation. Our experiments across several image classification benchmarks reveal which augmentation strategies provide the most consistent improvements in model generalization and robustness.

This work surveys and evaluates several explainable AI techniques applied to credit risk assessment models, including SHAP, LIME, and attention based interpretability methods. We conduct a comparative study on a real world lending dataset and analyze how well each method aligns with domain expert judgments regarding feature importance and decision rationale. We further extend our analysis with additional ablation studies and broader experimental comparisons.

title: Attention Mechanisms in Speech Recognition Systems (Extended Study)
abstract: Attention mechanisms have significantly advanced the performance of automatic speech recognition systems by allowing models to focus on relevant portions of the input sequence. In this paper we systematically compare different attention variants including additive, multiplicative, and multi head attention within an end to end speech recognition pipeline. Our results on standard speech benchmarks reveal that multi head attention provides the best trade off between recognition accuracy and computational efficiency. We further extend our analysis with additional ablation studies and broader experimental comparisons.

title: Unsupervised Anomaly Detection in Time Series Data Using Autoencoders (Extended Study)
abstract: Detecting anomalies in time series data is essential for applications ranging from industrial monitoring to fraud detection. We propose an unsupervised anomaly detection framework based on variational autoencoders that learns a compact latent representation of normal system behavior. Deviations from this learned representation are used to flag anomalous events. Experimental evaluation on multiple real world time series benchmarks demonstrates that our method achieves higher detection accuracy with fewer false positives compared to existing unsupervised approaches. We further extend our analysis with additional ablation studies and broader experimental comparisons.

title: Robotic Grasping Using Deep Learning and Tactile Feedback (Extended Study)
abstract: Reliable robotic grasping in unstructured environments remains a significant challenge in robotics research. This paper presents a deep learning framework that combines visual perception with tactile sensor feedback to improve grasp stability. We collect a large dataset of grasping attempts across diverse object shapes and materials to train our model. Real robot experiments show that incorporating tactile feedback substantially reduces grasp failures compared to vision only baselines. We further extend our analysis with additional ablation studies and broader experimental comparisons.

title: Sentiment Analysis of Social Media Text Using Deep Learning (Extended Study)
abstract: Sentiment analysis of social media content presents unique challenges due to informal language, slang, and short text length. This study proposes a hybrid deep learning model combining convolutional and recurrent layers to capture both local and sequential patterns in tweets. We evaluate our approach on several publicly available sentiment datasets and show that it outperforms traditional machine learning classifiers as well as standalone CNN and LSTM models. We further extend our analysis with additional ablation studies and broader experimental comparisons.

title: Bayesian Optimization for Hyperparameter Tuning of Deep Neural Networks (Extended Study)
abstract: Hyperparameter tuning is a critical yet computationally expensive step in training deep neural networks. This paper investigates the use of Bayesian optimization as an efficient alternative to grid search and random search for hyperparameter selection. We propose a surrogate model based on Gaussian processes combined with an acquisition function tailored for noisy objective evaluations. Experiments across several deep learning benchmarks demonstrate faster convergence to optimal hyperparameter configurations. We further extend our analysis with additional ablation studies and broader experimental comparisons.

title: Semantic Segmentation of Satellite Imagery Using Deep Learning (Extended Study)
abstract: Semantic segmentation of satellite imagery is important for applications such as land cover classification and urban planning. We propose a deep convolutional encoder decoder architecture with skip connections tailored to the multi spectral nature of satellite images. Our model is trained and evaluated on large scale remote sensing datasets, achieving improved segmentation accuracy for vegetation, water bodies, and built up areas compared to existing baseline architectures. We further extend our analysis with additional ablation studies and broader experimental comparisons.

title: Multi Agent Reinforcement Learning for Traffic Signal Control (Extended Study)
abstract: Efficient traffic signal control is essential for reducing urban congestion and emissions. This paper proposes a multi agent reinforcement learning framework in which each traffic signal is controlled by an independent learning agent that cooperates with neighboring agents through shared state information. Simulation results on a realistic urban traffic network show that our cooperative multi agent approach reduces average vehicle waiting time compared to independently trained agents and fixed time signal control baselines. We further extend our analysis with additional ablation studies and broader experimental comparisons.

title: Knowledge Graph Embedding Techniques for Recommendation Systems (Extended Study)
abstract: Knowledge graphs provide rich structured information that can enhance the performance of recommendation systems. In this work we survey several knowledge graph embedding techniques and evaluate their effectiveness when integrated into collaborative filtering based recommender models. Our experiments on benchmark recommendation datasets show that incorporating knowledge graph embeddings improves recommendation accuracy, particularly in cold start scenarios involving new users and items. We further extend our analysis with additional ablation studies and broader experimental comparisons.

title: Adversarial Robustness of Deep Learning Models for Image Classification (Extended Study)
abstract: Deep learning models for image classification are known to be vulnerable to adversarial perturbations that are imperceptible to humans. This paper studies several adversarial training techniques and evaluates their effectiveness at improving model robustness without significantly degrading clean accuracy. We conduct extensive experiments across multiple network architectures and adversarial attack methods, providing practical guidelines for training more robust image classification models. We further extend our analysis with additional ablation studies and broader experimental comparisons.

title: Few Shot Learning for Text Classification in Low Resource Languages (Extended Study)
abstract: Text classification in low resource languages is hindered by the scarcity of labeled training data. We propose a few shot learning approach that leverages cross lingual pretrained embeddings and meta learning to enable effective classification with only a handful of labeled examples per class. Experiments on multiple low resource language datasets demonstrate that our method significantly outperforms standard fine tuning approaches under limited data conditions. We further extend our analysis with additional ablation studies and broader experimental comparisons.

title: Neural Machine Translation with Improved Handling of Rare Words (Extended Study)
abstract: Neural machine translation systems often struggle with rare and out of vocabulary words, leading to degraded translation quality. This paper proposes a subword segmentation strategy combined with a copy mechanism that allows the model to directly transfer rare words from source to target sentences when appropriate. Evaluation on multiple language pairs shows consistent improvements in translation quality, particularly for domains with specialized or technical vocabulary. We further extend our analysis with additional ablation studies and broader experimental comparisons.

title: Time Series Forecasting Using Long Short Term Memory Networks (Extended Study)
abstract: Accurate time series forecasting is critical for applications such as demand planning and financial market analysis. This paper evaluates the performance of long short term memory networks for multivariate time series forecasting and compares them against traditional statistical models such as ARIMA. Our experiments on multiple real world datasets show that LSTM based models capture complex temporal dependencies more effectively, particularly for series exhibiting nonlinear and long range patterns. We further extend our analysis with additional ablation studies and broader experimental comparisons.

title: Data Augmentation Strategies for Improving Deep Learning Model Generalization (Extended Study)
abstract: Data augmentation is a widely used technique to improve the generalization ability of deep learning models, particularly when training data is limited. This paper presents a systematic comparison of various data augmentation strategies including geometric transformations, mixup, and generative adversarial network based augmentation. Our experiments across several image classification benchmarks reveal which augmentation strategies provide the most consistent improvements in model generalization and robustness. We further extend our analysis with additional ablation studies and broader experimental comparisons.

title: Deep Reinforcement Learning for Autonomous Robot Navigation (Extended Study)
abstract: This paper presents a deep reinforcement learning framework for autonomous navigation of mobile robots in dynamic and cluttered environments. We propose a novel reward shaping technique that accelerates convergence and improves policy stability. Extensive experiments in simulated and real world environments demonstrate that our approach outperforms classical path planning methods and prior learning based baselines in terms of success rate and collision avoidance. The proposed method generalizes well to unseen environments and shows robustness to sensor noise. We further extend our analysis with additional ablation studies and broader experimental comparisons.

title: A Transformer Based Approach for Scientific Text Summarization (Extended Study)
abstract: Automatic summarization of scientific literature is a challenging task due to the technical vocabulary and long document lengths involved. In this work we introduce a transformer based encoder decoder model fine tuned specifically for summarizing research papers. We evaluate our model on a large corpus of arXiv papers and show significant improvements over extractive and traditional abstractive baselines using ROUGE metrics. Human evaluation further confirms that the generated summaries are coherent and factually consistent with the source documents. We further extend our analysis with additional ablation studies and broader experimental comparisons.

title: Convolutional Neural Networks for Medical Image Classification (Extended Study)
abstract: Medical image classification plays a crucial role in computer aided diagnosis systems. In this study we design a convolutional neural network architecture optimized for classifying X-ray and MRI scans across multiple disease categories. Our model incorporates attention mechanisms to focus on clinically relevant regions of the image. Experimental results on multiple public medical imaging datasets show that our approach achieves state of the art accuracy while maintaining interpretability through visualization of attention maps. We further extend our analysis with additional ablation studies and broader experimental comparisons.

title: Graph Neural Networks for Social Network Analysis (Extended Study)
abstract: Graph neural networks have emerged as a powerful tool for modeling relational data such as social networks. This paper explores the application of graph convolutional networks to the tasks of community detection and link prediction in large scale social graphs. We propose a scalable training strategy that reduces memory consumption without sacrificing predictive performance. Our experiments on several benchmark social network datasets demonstrate superior performance compared to traditional graph embedding techniques. We further extend our analysis with additional ablation studies and broader experimental comparisons.

title: Natural Language Inference Using Pretrained Language Models (Extended Study)
abstract: Natural language inference is a fundamental task in natural language processing that requires determining the logical relationship between a premise and a hypothesis. We investigate the effectiveness of large pretrained transformer language models for this task and propose a fine tuning strategy that incorporates auxiliary linguistic features. Our experiments across several benchmark datasets show consistent improvements over baseline transformer models, particularly in cases involving negation and quantifier scope ambiguity. We further extend our analysis with additional ablation studies and broader experimental comparisons.

title: Federated Learning for Privacy Preserving Healthcare Analytics (Extended Study)
abstract: Federated learning enables collaborative model training across distributed healthcare institutions without sharing raw patient data, addressing critical privacy concerns. This paper proposes a federated learning framework tailored for heterogeneous electronic health record data. We introduce a personalization layer that adapts the global model to local data distributions at each institution. Experiments on multi institution clinical datasets show that our framework achieves comparable accuracy to centralized training while preserving patient privacy. We further extend our analysis with additional ablation studies and broader experimental comparisons.

This paper proposes a multi agent reinforcement learning framework in which each traffic signal is controlled by an independent learning agent that cooperates with neighboring agents through shared state information. Simulation results on a realistic urban traffic network show that our cooperative multi agent approach reduces average vehicle waiting time compared to independently trained agents and fixed time signal control baselines. We further extend our analysis with additional ablation studies and broader experimental comparisons.

title: Knowledge Graph Embedding Techniques for Recommendation Systems (Extended Study)
abstract: Knowledge graphs provide rich structured information that can enhance the performance of recommendation systems. In this work we survey several knowledge graph embedding techniques and evaluate their effectiveness when integrated into collaborative filtering based recommender models. Our experiments on benchmark recommendation datasets show that incorporating knowledge graph embeddings improves recommendation accuracy, particularly in cold start scenarios involving new users and items. We further extend our analysis with additional ablation studies and broader experimental comparisons.

title: Adversarial Robustness of Deep Learning Models for Image Classification (Extended Study)
abstract: Deep learning models for image classification are known to be vulnerable to adversarial perturbations that are imperceptible to humans. This paper studies several adversarial training techniques and evaluates their effectiveness at improving model robustness without significantly degrading clean accuracy. We conduct extensive experiments across multiple network architectures and adversarial attack methods, providing practical guidelines for training more robust image classification models. We further extend our analysis with additional ablation studies and broader experimental comparisons.

title: Few Shot Learning for Text Classification in Low Resource Languages (Extended Study)
abstract: Text classification in low resource languages is hindered by the scarcity of labeled training data. We propose a few shot learning approach that leverages cross lingual pretrained embeddings and meta learning to enable effective classification with only a handful of labeled examples per class. Experiments on multiple low resource language datasets demonstrate that our method significantly outperforms standard fine tuning approaches under limited data conditions. We further extend our analysis with additional ablation studies and broader experimental comparisons.

title: Neural Machine Translation with Improved Handling of Rare Words (Extended Study)
abstract: Neural machine translation systems often struggle with rare and out of vocabulary words, leading to degraded translation quality. This paper proposes a subword segmentation strategy combined with a copy mechanism that allows the model to directly transfer rare words from source to target sentences when appropriate. Evaluation on multiple language pairs shows consistent improvements in translation quality, particularly for domains with specialized or technical vocabulary. We further extend our analysis with additional ablation studies and broader experimental comparisons.

title: Time Series Forecasting Using Long Short Term Memory Networks (Extended Study)
abstract: Accurate time series forecasting is critical for applications such as demand planning and financial market analysis. This paper evaluates the performance of long short term memory networks for multivariate time series forecasting and compares them against traditional statistical models such as ARIMA. Our experiments on multiple real world datasets show that LSTM based models capture complex temporal dependencies more effectively, particularly for series exhibiting nonlinear and long range patterns. We further extend our analysis with additional ablation studies and broader experimental comparisons.

title: Data Augmentation Strategies for Improving Deep Learning Model Generalization (Extended Study)
abstract: Data augmentation is a widely used technique to improve the generalization ability of deep learning models, particularly when training data is limited. This paper presents a systematic comparison of various data augmentation strategies including geometric transformations, mixup, and generative adversarial network based augmentation. Our experiments across several image classification benchmarks reveal which augmentation strategies provide the most consistent improvements in model generalization and robustness. We further extend our analysis with additional ablation studies and broader experimental comparisons.

title: Deep Reinforcement Learning for Autonomous Robot Navigation (Extended Study)
abstract: This paper presents a deep reinforcement learning framework for autonomous navigation of mobile robots in dynamic and cluttered environments. We propose a novel reward shaping technique that accelerates convergence and improves policy stability. Extensive experiments in simulated and real world environments demonstrate that our approach outperforms classical path planning methods and prior learning based baselines in terms of success rate and collision avoidance. The proposed method generalizes well to unseen environments and shows robustness to sensor noise. We further extend our analysis with additional ablation studies and broader experimental comparisons.

title: A Transformer Based Approach for Scientific Text Summarization (Extended Study)
abstract: Automatic summarization of scientific literature is a challenging task due to the technical vocabulary and long document lengths involved. In this work we introduce a transformer based encoder decoder model fine tuned specifically for summarizing research papers. We evaluate our model on a large corpus of arXiv papers and show significant improvements over extractive and traditional abstractive baselines using ROUGE metrics. Human evaluation further confirms that the generated summaries are coherent and factually consistent with the source documents. We further extend our analysis with additional ablation studies and broader experimental comparisons.

title: Convolutional Neural Networks for Medical Image Classification (Extended Study)
abstract: Medical image classification plays a crucial role in computer aided diagnosis systems. In this study we design a convolutional neural network architecture optimized for classifying X-ray and MRI scans across multiple disease categories. Our model incorporates attention mechanisms to focus on clinically relevant regions of the image. Experimental results on multiple public medical imaging datasets show that our approach achieves state of the art accuracy while maintaining interpretability through visualization of attention maps. We further extend our analysis with additional ablation studies and broader experimental comparisons.

title: Graph Neural Networks for Social Network Analysis (Extended Study)
abstract: Graph neural networks have emerged as a powerful tool for modeling relational data such as social networks. This paper explores the application of graph convolutional networks to the tasks of community detection and link prediction in large scale social graphs. We propose a scalable training strategy that reduces memory consumption without sacrificing predictive performance. Our experiments on several benchmark social network datasets demonstrate superior performance compared to traditional graph embedding techniques. We further extend our analysis with additional ablation studies and broader experimental comparisons.

title: Natural Language Inference Using Pretrained Language Models (Extended Study)
abstract: Natural language inference is a fundamental task in natural language processing that requires determining the logical relationship between a premise and a hypothesis. We investigate the effectiveness of large pretrained transformer language models for this task and propose a fine tuning strategy that incorporates auxiliary linguistic features. Our experiments across several benchmark datasets show consistent improvements over baseline transformer models, particularly in cases involving negation and quantifier scope ambiguity. We further extend our analysis with additional ablation studies and broader experimental comparisons.

title: Federated Learning for Privacy Preserving Healthcare Analytics (Extended Study)
abstract: Federated learning enables collaborative model training across distributed healthcare institutions without sharing raw patient data, addressing critical privacy concerns. This paper proposes a federated learning framework tailored for heterogeneous electronic health record data. We introduce a personalization layer that adapts the global model to local data distributions at each institution. Experiments on multi institution clinical datasets show that our framework achieves comparable accuracy to centralized training while preserving patient privacy. We further extend our analysis with additional ablation studies and broader experimental comparisons.

title: Explainable AI Methods for Credit Risk Assessment (Extended Study)
abstract: As machine learning models are increasingly deployed in high stakes financial decisions, the need for explainability has become paramount. This work surveys and evaluates several explainable AI techniques applied to credit risk assessment models, including SHAP, LIME, and attention based interpretability methods. We conduct a comparative study on a real world lending dataset and analyze how well each method aligns with domain expert judgments regarding feature importance and decision rationale. We further extend our analysis with additional ablation studies and broader experimental comparisons.

title: Attention Mechanisms in Speech Recognition Systems (Extended Study)
abstract: Attention mechanisms have significantly advanced the performance of automatic speech recognition systems by allowing models to focus on relevant portions of the input sequence. In this paper we systematically compare different attention variants including additive, multiplicative, and multi head attention within an end to end speech recognition pipeline. Our results on standard speech benchmarks reveal that multi head attention provides the best trade off between recognition accuracy and computational efficiency. We further extend our analysis with additional ablation studies and broader experimental comparisons.

title: Unsupervised Anomaly Detection in Time Series Data Using Autoencoders (Extended Study)
abstract: Detecting anomalies in time series data is essential for applications ranging from industrial monitoring to fraud detection. We propose an unsupervised anomaly detection framework based on variational autoencoders that learns a compact latent representation of normal system behavior. Deviations from this learned representation are used to flag anomalous events. Experimental evaluation on multiple real world time series benchmarks demonstrates that our method achieves higher detection accuracy with fewer false positives compared to existing unsupervised approaches. We further extend our analysis with additional ablation studies and broader experimental comparisons.

title: Robotic Grasping Using Deep Learning and Tactile Feedback (Extended Study)
abstract: Reliable robotic grasping in unstructured environments remains a significant challenge in robotics research. This paper presents a deep learning framework that combines visual perception with tactile sensor feedback to improve grasp stability. We collect a large dataset of grasping attempts across diverse object shapes and materials to train our model. Real robot experiments show that incorporating tactile feedback substantially reduces grasp failures compared to vision only baselines. We further extend our analysis with additional ablation studies and broader experimental comparisons.

title: Sentiment Analysis of Social Media Text Using Deep Learning (Extended Study)
abstract: Sentiment analysis of social media content presents unique challenges due to informal language, slang, and short text length. This study proposes a hybrid deep learning model combining convolutional and recurrent layers to capture both local and sequential patterns in tweets. We evaluate our approach on several publicly available sentiment datasets and show that it outperforms traditional machine learning classifiers as well as standalone CNN and LSTM models. We further extend our analysis with additional ablation studies and broader experimental comparisons.

title: Bayesian Optimization for Hyperparameter Tuning of Deep Neural Networks (Extended Study)
abstract: Hyperparameter tuning is a critical yet computationally expensive step in training deep neural networks. This paper investigates the use of Bayesian optimization as an efficient alternative to grid search and random search for hyperparameter selection. We propose a surrogate model based on Gaussian processes combined with an acquisition function tailored for noisy objective evaluations. Experiments across several deep learning benchmarks demonstrate faster convergence to optimal hyperparameter configurations. We further extend our analysis with additional ablation studies and broader experimental comparisons.

title: Semantic Segmentation of Satellite Imagery Using Deep Learning (Extended Study)
abstract: Semantic segmentation of satellite imagery is important for applications such as land cover classification and urban planning. We propose a deep convolutional encoder decoder architecture with skip connections tailored to the multi spectral nature of satellite images. Our model is trained and evaluated on large scale remote sensing datasets, achieving improved segmentation accuracy for vegetation, water bodies, and built up areas compared to existing baseline architectures. We further extend our analysis with additional ablation studies and broader experimental comparisons.
